mechanism_name: Tokyo-morning range contraction -> London-morning expansion breakout (intraday-only, flat before NY rollover)

economic_mechanism.summary: Asian hours for the European-quoted majors are structurally quiet (documented intraday FX volatility periodicity: Andersen & Bollerslev 1997). Stop-loss and option-barrier orders accumulate just outside the visible Tokyo-night range. When London opens, dealer hedging and stop-trigger flow turn a range compression into directional expansion; entries that join the first completed-bar close beyond the Tokyo range ride triggered-stop momentum flow (Osler 2005: clustered stop-loss orders produce self-reinforcing price cascades in FX) and exit the same NY day before rollover.
economic_mechanism.profit_source: directional continuation during the London-open / NY-morning liquidity expansion following a quiet Tokyo-night compression
economic_mechanism.loss_source: failed breakouts: London flow rejects the extreme and mean-reverts back inside the range; the losing trade's counterparty is the range-fader
economic_mechanism.why_h1_bars_suffice: the range and its violation are both defined on completed hourly bars; the mechanism is a multi-hour session event, not a tick-level microstructure event
economic_mechanism.no_volume_claim: mechanism uses prices only; FX volume is decentralized and is never used

expected_counterparty.on_winning_trades: (a) stop-loss orders resting beyond the Tokyo range extremes (Osler 2005: stop clusters trigger cascades - we join the cascade late, capturing its continuation); (b) dealers hedging into triggered-stop flow at the London open
expected_counterparty.on_losing_trades: range-fade liquidity providers who sell/buy the London extension back inside the Tokyo range
expected_counterparty.why_they_let_us_win: stop clusters are mechanical and price-insensitive; someone must take the other side of them, and the cascade they trigger persists for hours, longer than our intraday holding window

signal_fields: twelvedata H1 open/high/low/close, UTC-stamped, completed canonical bars only (bar datetime = bar OPEN instant; bar is actionable only at open_instant + 1h = completion instant)
signal_fields_and_publication_clock.publication_clock: each completed H1 bar publishes at its completion instant (open stamp + 1h); signals are computed once per completion instant and never revised; the decision instant is always strictly before the fill instant (next allowed bar open)
signal_fields_and_publication_clock.session_labels: Tokyo window keyed to Asia/Tokyo wall clock (no DST in Japan -> fixed 00:00-06:00 UTC year-round); breakout window keyed to Europe/London wall clock (UK DST via zoneinfo); flatten boundary keyed to America/New_York wall clock (US DST via zoneinfo)

entry_exit_and_rollover_flat_rule.range_construction_completed_bars_only: For each Tokyo business day D: take the completed H1 bars whose open instants map to [09:00, 15:00) Asia/Tokyo wall clock on D (stamps 09,10,11,12,13,14 JST; exactly 6 bars). AH = max(high), AL = min(low), W = AH - AL. If fewer than 6 canonical in-calendar bars exist in the window, the day is structurally INVALID and no trade may initiate (this excludes every Monday, because Mon 09:00-10:00 JST precedes the Sun 21:00 America/New_York weekly open; this is a calendar fact, not a choice).
entry_exit_and_rollover_flat_rule.entry_signal: Completed-bar decision window: bars whose open instants map to [08:00, 12:00) Europe/London (stamps 08,09,10,11 London). On each such completed bar B in chronological order: LONG signal if close(B) > AH (strict); SHORT signal if close(B) < AL (strict); first signal of the day only, opposite side permanently cancelled for that day; no signal by end of window = no trade.
entry_exit_and_rollover_flat_rule.entry_execution: next-allowed-bar: fill at the open of the first canonical calendar bar whose open instant is strictly after B's completion instant, provided that open instant maps to a NY wall-clock time strictly before 15:00 America/New_York; otherwise the signal is discarded (flatten rule takes precedence)
exits: stop exit: on any completed bar C after the fill, LONG if close(C) < AL (strict), SHORT if close(C) > AH (strict) -> fill at the open of the next allowed bar (same 15:00 NY cutoff); this structural opposite-extreme stop is the only risk exit; there is no profit target

mandatory flatten: any position still open exits with fill at the open of the H1 bar stamped 15:00 America/New_York (bar completion 16:00 NY, two full hours strictly before the 17:00 NY rollover instant); identical rule on Friday, where the 15:00 NY bar is the last bar of the week (weekly close Fri 16:00 NY per the frozen calendar)
entry_exit_and_rollover_flat_rule.rollover_flat_invariant: no fill may execute at a bar open at or after 15:00 America/New_York; therefore the book is flat from 15:00 NY wall clock, strictly before every 17:00 NY rollover instant under any bar-stamping convention; positions never span a rollover instant, never span the weekend; financing exposure is zero by construction (no financing data used or needed)
entry_exit_and_rollover_flat_rule.one_position_rule: at most one position per NY trading day, no re-entry after a stop, no stop-and-reverse

execution_model.signals: completed H1 bars only; no intrabar trigger fills; a close beyond a level is detected at bar completion
execution_model.fills: always at the OPEN price of the next allowed canonical bar; gaps fill at the open (no assumption of a fill at the trigger level AH/AL); market-order semantics; no limit orders, no partial fills
execution_model.allowed_bar: a canonical, deduped H1 bar of the frozen trading-week calendar (Sun 21:00 America/New_York -> Fri 16:00 America/New_York, DST-correct via zoneinfo); the canonical series contains no weekend bars
execution_model.data_gap_rule_fail_conservative: if the fill bar for an ENTRY is missing, the order is cancelled; if a fill bar for an EXIT is missing, the exit executes at the first available later bar open and the event is logged as a data-gap breach to be reconciled by A7; an exit later than the 15:00 NY boundary is never silently accepted
execution_model.no_assumptions: no bid/ask (proxy spread exists only inside the frozen cost stress), no volume, no rollover/financing data, no leverage, no intrabar path assumptions

frozen_cost_stress_matrix.definition: round-trip cost in price basis points charged once per completed round trip: net_log_return = log(exit_open / entry_open) - cost_bps * 1e-4; proxy spread is a CONSERVATIVE STRESS INPUT, never a live-spread claim
frozen_cost_stress_matrix.one_event_delay_stress: every execution (entry, stop exit, flatten) shifted one additional completed bar later; a delayed exit that would land at or after the 15:00 NY boundary collapses into the 15:00 NY flatten fill, so the delay never violates the flat invariant
frozen_cost_stress_matrix.rationale: proxies are set at roughly twice typical ECN all-in round-trip costs for these majors (UNVERIFIED practitioner levels, frozen for stress only); x2.0 is the survival condition

pair_universe.window: 2020-01-29 -> 2026-09-02 H1 canonical (approx 6.59y per pair), all 7 pairs evaluated identically
pair_universe.preregistered_heterogeneity_prediction: USD/JPY's 'Tokyo morning' is its home liquidity session, not a quiet window; the mechanism should therefore be weakest on USD/JPY and strongest on EUR/USD, GBP/USD, USD/CHF. This sub-prediction is evaluated but NOT a kill rule.

anchor.definition: exactly the mechanism in entry_exit_and_rollover_flat_rule: Tokyo range [09:00,15:00) JST (6 bars), London decision window [08:00,12:00) London (4 bars), opposite-extreme stop, 15:00 NY flatten
anchor.why_it_validates: if the London-open stop-cascade / expansion mechanism is real, completed-bar closes beyond a quiet Tokyo range should be followed by directional continuation that survives the frozen conservative cost matrix

neighbour.definition: single preregistered adjacent variant: Tokyo range widened by one bar on each side, [08:00,16:00) JST (8 bars); every other element identical
neighbour.why_it_validates: tests boundary sensitivity: a real session-structure mechanism degrades gracefully when the range window moves by one bar; a data-mined artifact typically flips sign or collapses
neighbour.why_more_variants_are_forbidden: any additional window would be a grid; the neighbour is fixed here, before any returns exist

negative_control.definition: identical rule on the identical range (same AH/AL from the same Tokyo bars, same completed-close breakout logic, same execution and 15:00 NY flatten), but entries restricted to completed bars stamped in [18:00, 21:00) America/New_York - the deep Asian quiet window for these pairs
negative_control.why_it_destroys: the mechanism's claim is session timing: expansion follows the London open, not the range level itself. Documented FX intraday volatility periodicity (Andersen & Bollerslev 1997) puts near-minimum activity in this control window. If the same breakout signal carries equal-or-greater net expectancy in the quiet window, the session-timing story is false - the rule is generic breakout beta - and the anchor is rejected
negative_control.causality_note: the control holds the signal constant and moves only the session hour of execution, isolating the timing channel

falsification_rule.scope: evaluated only in the later authorized phase on the full canonical H1 window per pair; nothing here computes or inspects returns
falsification_rule.statistic_per_pair_per_arm: per-trade net log return (bps) under the stated stress cell; summary = mean trade expectancy with day-clustered t-stat, plus trade count

kills.K1_viability: FAIL if fewer than 4 of 7 pairs have mean net trade expectancy > 0 at stress x1.0/no-delay, OR fewer than 4 of 7 at x1.5/one-bar-delay, OR any pair below -5 bps/trade at x1.5/one-bar-delay
kills.K2_session_causality: FAIL if anchor mean net expectancy (x1.0/no-delay) does not exceed the negative control's in at least 5 of 7 pairs
kills.K3_neighbour_robustness: FAIL if Spearman rank correlation of anchor vs neighbour mean net expectancy across the 7 pairs is below +0.5
kills.K4_cost_fragility: FAIL if the sign of mean net expectancy differs between x1.0 and x2.0 in 4 or more pairs

falsification_rule.survival_condition: K1 AND K2 AND K3 AND NOT K4 all hold; any other outcome falsifies the proposal as specified; no re-specification, no parameter rescue, no window change permitted after any return is visible
falsification_rule.no_grid_search: anchors contain zero free parameters; the single neighbour is preregistered; no other configuration is evaluable under this proposal

expected_regimes.favours: post-compression expansion days; London/NY trend days; macro-surprise weeks with stop cascades at session opens; normal-liquidity Tue-Thu
expected_regimes.adverse: holiday-thinned weeks; persistent chop around the range edge (whipsaw at x1.5+ costs); regimes where Asian hours carry the volatility (JPY-centered shocks - preregistered USD/JPY weakness); low-range regimes where stop clusters sit inside noise
expected_regimes.structural_bounds_not_results: at most one trade per invalid-Monday-excluded NY trading day; expected order of magnitude 300-900 trades/pair over 6.59y - design bounds only, no returns computed here

dst_session_clock_spec.frozen_calendar: trading week Sunday 21:00 America/New_York open -> Friday 16:00 America/New_York close; daily rollover 17:00 America/New_York; all boundaries computed via zoneinfo named zones (DST-correct), matching DEFAULT_FX_WEEK_CONVENTION in research/assets/forex/sessions.py
dst_session_clock_spec.bar_labeling: each canonical H1 bar is labeled by its UTC open instant; NY / London / Tokyo wall-clock labels are derived per bar via zoneinfo (America/New_York, Europe/London, Asia/Tokyo); UTC->zone mapping is single-valued so DST fall-back is unambiguous
dst_session_clock_spec.transition_days: US transitions occur ~02:00 local Sunday and UK transitions ~01:00 UTC Sunday: both fall outside all Mon-Fri session windows used here, so no session window is ever truncated by a DST transition on a trading day
dst_session_clock_spec.flatten_boundary: 15:00 America/New_York wall-clock bar open (bar completion 16:00 NY), i.e. strictly before the 17:00 NY rollover by two full hours in both EST and EDT

data_fields_used: bar open timestamp (UTC) for session mapping via zoneinfo
data_fields_explicitly_not_used: volume (null in canonical series; centralized FX volume forbidden)
any other provider, any fundamental/macro series
